item.title: Quick Fire 🔥 with Udeme Jalekun
item.description: Meet Udeme Jalekun, a Senior Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer, who has delivered quality across more than 10 major fintech and social-impact products, including SwervePay, Geegpay, Quickteller Paypoint, and Kippa Pay.

item.title: “Where there’s mystery, there’s margin”: How fintech twin brothers built WapiPay
item.description: The story they begin telling stretches back much further than their shared vision at WapiPay. Eddie and Paul trace it back to a moment of grief that arrived early in their lives.

item.title: Chukwuemeka Afigbo says Africa’s deep tech problem is structural. He’s already fixing it.
item.description: Chukwuemeka Afigbo is making a long-term bet: Africa’s most ambitious technologists are not constrained by a shortage of ideas, but by a shortage of structured pathways.

item.title: Kenyan rights group wants Meta’s smart glasses footage investigated
item.description: The Oversight Labs, a Kenyan digital rights group, has asked the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC) to investigate whether footage captured by Ray-Ban Meta Smart Glasses is being used unlawfully to train artificial intelligence systems.

item.title: Nigeria exited the FATF grey list. Now it wants to set the rules for African fintech
item.description: After two years of coordinated reforms, Nigeria has cleared one of the biggest reputational hurdles in its financial history. The CBN’s new fintech report signals what comes next: not just cleaning up, but leading the line. For years, the most expensive cost for many Nigerian fintechs was not a licensing fee or a compliance audit. […]

item.title: 69% of Africa’s biometric fintech fraud is now AI-generated, says report
item.description: Rather than create fake identities to open new accounts, fraudsters prefer to hijack existing, verified ones, exposing a blind spot in systems that were built on the assumption that the main risk sits at signup, not months later inside live accounts.

item.title: Kenyan court strikes down law criminalising false information online
item.description: Kenya’s Court of Appeal struck down “false information” offences in the Cybercrimes Act, ruling the provisions unconstitutional.

item.title: “We are building on top of an immature ecosystem”: Day 1-1000 of Bujeti
item.description: That observation, made in 2021, became Bujeti that same year, a Lagos-based fintech that has since grown into what its founders call a finance control centre for African businesses.

item.title: Digital Nomads: A new visa wants to lure short-term travellers to South Africa
item.description: South Africa wants to become Africa’s events capital, but its visa system has long frustrated travellers and conference delegates. A new programme called MEETS promises faster, bulk visa processing.

item.title: Passported out: How Africa grounds its own leaders
item.description: Our data shows that a pan-African consultant earns 5x more than a domestic-only practitioner. The difference isn't the CV; it’s the passport.
